views.name: patient_basic_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Patient.ID AS ID,
  Patient.SEX AS SEX,
  Patient.Admission AS Admission,
  Patient.Birthday AS Birthday
FROM Patient

params.description: Provides one-row-per-patient basic demographic fields (sex, admission date, birthday) for each Patient.ID.
params.when_to_use: Lookup demographic attributes for a specific patient ID or set of patient IDs | Join patient demographics to clinical events or measurements while maintaining patient-level grain | Compose patient-level cohorts (e.g., filter patients by sex or admission date range) before aggregating outcomes
params.output_schema: ID: unique patient identifier — derived from Patient.ID | SEX: patient sex/gender code/value — derived from Patient.SEX | Admission: patient admission datetime/date — derived from Patient.Admission | Birthday: patient birth date/datetime — derived from Patient.Birthday
params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Patient.SEX | Patient.Admission | Patient.Birthday
params.metric: ID = direct column (no aggregation) — Patient.ID | SEX = direct column (no aggregation) — Patient.SEX | Admission = direct column (no aggregation) — Patient.Admission | Birthday = direct column (no aggregation) — Patient.Birthday
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient-level dimensions or lookup tables on Patient.ID (e.g., join to another one-row-per-patient view on ID) — safe because this view is one-row-per-Patient.ID so measures/columns remain 1:1 and are not duplicated. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many event/measurement tables (e.g., clinical events, orders, lab results keyed by patient and event id) without aggregation on the many-side first — such joins would multiply patient rows and thus duplicate patient-level fields/metrics. | If joining to a one-to-many table, first aggregate the many-side to patient-level (e.g., count of events per Patient.ID, max(date) per Patient.ID) and then join on Patient.ID to preserve correct cardinality. | If the underlying Patient table can contain duplicate Patient.ID rows (contrary to declared grain), deduplicate or aggregate (e.g., choose MIN/MAX for Admission/Birthday) on Patient.ID before joining; as provided, this view assumes Patient.ID is unique and returns one row per ID.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-patient basic demographic fields (sex, admission date, birthday) for each Patient.ID.
validated_on: List the patient ID, sex and birthday of patient with LDH beyond normal range.

views.name: patient_admission_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  SEX,
  Admission
FROM
  patient_basic_demographics
WHERE
  Admission IS NOT NULL
  AND SEX IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides a cohort of admitted patients at the row (patient) level with their sex and admission status — i.e., which patients have a non-null Admission value and known sex.
params.when_to_use: List-level reporting or filtering of patients who have an Admission value and known SEX (e.g., create downstream cohorts) | Joining patient-level demographics (sex) to other patient-level data where only admitted patients should be considered | Composing higher-level aggregates (counts by SEX, rates among admitted patients) by aggregating this view
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier (derived directly from patient_basic_demographics.ID) | SEX: patient sex/gender value (derived directly from patient_basic_demographics.SEX) | Admission: admission indicator or admission-related value (derived directly from patient_basic_demographics.Admission)
params.grounded_columns: patient_basic_demographics.ID | patient_basic_demographics.SEX | patient_basic_demographics.Admission
params.metric: ID = identity(patient_basic_demographics.ID) | SEX = identity(patient_basic_demographics.SEX) | Admission = identity(patient_basic_demographics.Admission) | count_patients = COUNT(ID)  -- can be computed by aggregating this view; the view itself is at patient-grain so no aggregation is pre-applied
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional or one-row-per-patient tables/views (for example, patient_basic_demographics (if used as a canonical patient row) or other one-row-per-patient views) on ID — safe because patient_admission_cohort is one-row-per-ID (the SQL selects ID directly and filters rows, not aggregating), so joining on ID to another one-row-per-ID source will not duplicate rows/measures. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (for example, encounters, diagnoses, orders, or any table that can have multiple rows per ID) without re-aggregation or de-duplication first — doing so will multiply this view's patient rows and any downstream counts derived from it. If you need patient-level measures combined with many-rows-per-patient data, first aggregate the many-rows-per-patient source to one row per ID (e.g., COUNT(encounter_id) AS encounters_per_patient) and then join on ID. | When composing aggregations: to compute counts by SEX, run SELECT SEX, COUNT(ID) FROM patient_admission_cohort GROUP BY SEX — this is safe and accurate because the view is already at patient grain. | If you need to enrich this cohort with time-varying or repeated-event data, prefer lateral/exists/subquery patterns or pre-aggregated derived tables keyed by ID to avoid accidental row multiplication.

views.description: Provides a cohort of admitted patients at the row (patient) level with their sex and admission status — i.e., which patients have a non-null Admission value and known sex.

views.name: patient_admission_counts_by_sex
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(p.SEX, '') AS SEX,
  COALESCE(p.Admission, '') AS Admission,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count,
  NULL AS ID_placeholder
FROM patient_basic_demographics p
GROUP BY
  COALESCE(p.SEX, ''),
  COALESCE(p.Admission, '')

params.description: Counts of distinct patients grouped by SEX and Admission status.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of unique patients for each combination of SEX and Admission values. | Build higher-level aggregates by SEX or by Admission (e.g., total patients by SEX across all Admission values). | Join as a pre-aggregated metric source when composing dashboards or further SQL that needs patient counts by SEX and Admission without re-counting individuals.
params.output_schema: SEX: categorical sex value used for grouping; derived from patient_basic_demographics.SEX with NULLs coerced to empty string via COALESCE(p.SEX, '') | Admission: categorical admission value used for grouping; derived from patient_basic_demographics.Admission with NULLs coerced to empty string via COALESCE(p.Admission, '') | patient_count: distinct patient count for the (SEX, Admission) group; derived as COUNT(DISTINCT patient_basic_demographics.ID)
params.grounded_columns: patient_basic_demographics.SEX | patient_basic_demographics.Admission | patient_basic_demographics.ID
params.metric: patient_count = COUNT(DISTINCT patient_basic_demographics.ID)  -- distinct-count aggregate over ID per (SEX, Admission)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables or views keyed exactly to SEX or Admission (or both) — for example, join to a SEX lookup or Admission-type dimension on SEX and/or Admission. Safe because this view is one row per (SEX, Admission) group, so joining to a one-row-per-key dimension will not duplicate patient_count. | You may aggregate this view up to a coarser grain (e.g., sum patient_count by SEX alone or by Admission alone) — summation is correct because patient_count is a distinct-count already rolled up to the view's grain. | Do NOT join this view directly to any table or view that is one-to-many keyed to (SEX, Admission) without first aggregating that other table to the same (SEX, Admission) grain. Example: do not join to a detailed encounters table keyed by patient encounter_id (many encounters per patient) unless you either (a) aggregate encounters to (SEX, Admission) before joining, or (b) join on patient ID and carefully deduplicate, because joining raw one-to-many detail will multiply rows and inflate patient_count. | Do NOT join to patient_basic_demographics (the same underlying table) on non-unique keys expecting counts to remain correct — joining back to the source detail rows without re-aggregation can duplicate counts. If you need additional patient attributes, join on patient ID to a deduplicated patient-level table or subquery (one row per patient) so patient_count is not multiplied. | If composing with sibling view patient_admission_cohort (SEL) or other cohort filters, apply cohort filtering at the patient level before computing distinct ID counts, or re-compute the distinct count after joining the cohort; joining this aggregated view to a cohort selection that is many-to-many with (SEX, Admission) can lead to incorrect duplication of patient_count unless the cohort is aggregated to the same grain.

views.description: Counts of distinct patients grouped by SEX and Admission status.

views.name: examination_by_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Examination.ID AS "ID",
  Examination."Examination Date" AS "Examination Date",
  Examination."Diagnosis" AS "Diagnosis",
  Examination."Thrombosis" AS "Thrombosis",
  Examination."aCL IgG" AS "aCL IgG",
  Examination."aCL IgM" AS "aCL IgM",
  Examination."ANA" AS "ANA",
  Examination."ANA Pattern" AS "ANA Pattern"
FROM Examination

params.description: Provides one row per clinical examination for a patient, returning the exam date and a set of diagnosis/test-result columns (Diagnosis, Thrombosis, aCL IgG, aCL IgM, ANA, ANA Pattern).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve examination-level clinical details for patients (e.g., list all exams and reported diagnostic/test fields). | Filter or group analyses by individual examination date or examination ID before composing further aggregations. | Join examination-level attributes to patient-level cohorts when you need exam-specific values (for example, most-recent exam results or exam counts by result type after proper aggregation). | Serve as the base for metrics that count examinations satisfying conditions (e.g., count of exams with positive ANA) — but only after aggregating, not by directly joining to many-sided tables.
params.output_schema: ID: Examination.ID — unique identifier of the examination (base column Examination.ID). | Examination Date: Examination."Examination Date" — the date (or datetime) of the examination (base column Examination."Examination Date"). | Diagnosis: Examination."Diagnosis" — diagnosis recorded on this examination (base column Examination."Diagnosis"). | Thrombosis: Examination."Thrombosis" — thrombosis field recorded on this examination (base column Examination."Thrombosis"). | aCL IgG: Examination."aCL IgG" — anticardiolipin IgG test value recorded on this examination (base column Examination."aCL IgG"). | aCL IgM: Examination."aCL IgM" — anticardiolipin IgM test value recorded on this examination (base column Examination."aCL IgM"). | ANA: Examination."ANA" — antinuclear antibody (ANA) test value for this examination (base column Examination."ANA"). | ANA Pattern: Examination."ANA Pattern" — ANA pattern reported for this examination (base column Examination."ANA Pattern").
params.grounded_columns: Examination.ID | Examination."Examination Date" | Examination."Diagnosis" | Examination."Thrombosis" | Examination."aCL IgG" | Examination."aCL IgM" | Examination."ANA" | Examination."ANA Pattern"
params.metric: This view exposes no pre-aggregated metrics; all columns are direct projections of base columns. Example derived metrics you can compute on top of this view (must be defined when composing): | examination_count = COUNT(ID)  -- number of examinations (aggregate over this view, grouping as needed) | exams_with_positive_ANA = SUM(CASE WHEN "ANA" = 'positive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- example predicate-based count (predicate must match stored values) | most_recent_exam_date_per_patient = MAX("Examination Date")  -- requires grouping by patient identifier (not present in this view) or joining to a patient key first
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to patient-level dimensions or views on a column that is one-to-one with Examination.ID (if such a patient key is exposed) — safe because this view is one-row-per Examination.ID so joining to a one-row-per-patient table requires aggregating or selecting a single exam per patient first. | cardinality-SAFE: join to patient_admission_cohort (SEL) on a patient_id key (if patient_admission_cohort provides patient-level rows) only after aggregating this view to patient-level (for example, using MAX("Examination Date") or COUNT(ID) grouped by patient). Do NOT join patient_admission_cohort directly to this view AND also to another one-to-many table without aggregation, because that would multiply rows. | DO NOT join this view to other tables/views that are one-to-many with Examination.ID (for example, a table of multiple exam observations keyed by Examination.ID) without re-aggregating those many-rows back to one row per Examination.ID first — otherwise measures like COUNT(ID) or other derived counts will be inflated by duplication. | DO NOT assume this view contains a patient identifier. If you need patient-level composition (e.g., counts per patient), first join the Examination table or another view that provides the patient key, or aggregate this view after adding the patient key to ensure correct grouping. | When composing aggregates across this view and sibling AGG views (like patient_admission_counts_by_sex), ensure at least one side of any join is pre-aggregated to the intended grain. For example, to compute admissions-by-exam metrics, aggregate examinations to patient or admission grain before joining to patient_admission_counts_by_sex; otherwise admissions counts can be duplicated.

views.description: Provides one row per clinical examination for a patient, returning the exam date and a set of diagnosis/test-result columns (Diagnosis, Thrombosis, aCL IgG, aCL IgM, ANA, ANA Pattern).

views.name: female_patient_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  SEX,
  Birthday
FROM
  Patient
WHERE
  SEX = 'F'

params.description: Returns the cohort of patients who are female, at the patient (ID) grain, including sex and birthday.
params.when_to_use: List all female patients and their basic demographics | Filter other analyses to only female patients by joining on patient ID | Build further patient-level aggregates restricted to female patients (must re-aggregate after joining to one-to-many tables) | Validate counts or demographics for the female subset of the Patient table
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier — derives directly from Patient.ID | SEX: patient sex value — derives directly from Patient.SEX (constant 'F' for all rows in this view) | Birthday: patient birth date — derives directly from Patient.Birthday
params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Patient.SEX | Patient.Birthday
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*) over the view's result set (patient-level count of female patients) | Note: there are no aggregate metrics defined inside this SELECT; any aggregates needed when composing must be computed by the consumer from the view's rows (for example COUNT(ID) to get number of female patients).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_basic_demographics (NORM) on ID — safe because both are one-row-per-ID patient-level views/tables, so this view's patient-level measures/rows will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_admission_cohort (SEL) on ID only if patient_admission_cohort is guaranteed to be one-row-per-ID; if patient_admission_cohort is one-row-per-admission (one-to-many), joining directly will multiply patient rows — in that case aggregate admissions (e.g., COUNT(admission_id) grouped by ID) before joining or join from admissions and then re-aggregate back to patient-level. | do NOT join directly to patient_admission_counts_by_sex (AGG) on ID without understanding its grain — if that view is aggregated by sex (or by sex and other dimensions) it may be multi-row-per-ID or not keyed by ID; instead join on SEX or join to an ID-keyed pre-aggregated result. Joining an AGG that is one-to-many relative to ID will multiply rows/measures. | do NOT join directly to examination_by_patient (SEL) without re-aggregation — examination_by_patient is likely one-to-many (multiple examinations per patient). If you join it directly to this patient-level view you will duplicate patient rows. Instead, aggregate examinations to patient-level (e.g., COUNT(exam_id) GROUP BY ID) and then join on ID, or perform analyses starting from examination_by_patient and filter via this view using an INNER JOIN or WHERE EXISTS ensuring proper grouping. | general rule: this view is strictly one-row-per-Patient.ID (grain = ID). It is safe to join to other tables or views that are also one-row-per-ID (dimensions) on ID without duplicating rows. For any one-to-many relationships (admissions, examinations, events), either aggregate the many-side to patient-level before joining, or join and then re-aggregate back to patient-level to avoid multiplying counts/measures.

views.description: Returns the cohort of patients who are female, at the patient (ID) grain, including sex and birthday.

views.name: patient_cohort_by_admission_and_diagnosis
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Patient.ID AS ID,
  Patient.Admission AS Admission,
  Patient.Diagnosis AS Diagnosis
FROM Patient

params.description: Lists one row per patient with that patient's admission and primary diagnosis — useful for cohort selection and as a base for composing admission- or diagnosis-focused analyses.
params.when_to_use: Select a cohort of patients by Admission or Diagnosis (filtering, counts of distinct patients). | Join patient-level admission/diagnosis attributes onto other patient-level facts without changing row cardinality. | Serve as the seed/lookup for building aggregates by Admission or Diagnosis when aggregated after safe joins.
params.output_schema: ID: unique patient identifier — derives from Patient.ID | Admission: patient admission attribute (e.g., admission date or admission code depending on source) — derives from Patient.Admission | Diagnosis: patient primary diagnosis attribute (e.g., diagnosis code or text) — derives from Patient.Diagnosis
params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Patient.Admission | Patient.Diagnosis
params.metric: ID = Patient.ID | Admission = Patient.Admission | Diagnosis = Patient.Diagnosis
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables or views that are one-row-per-ID on ID — e.g., join to patient_basic_demographics(NORM) on ID — safe because both are one-row-per-patient and will not duplicate this view's rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_admission_cohort(SEL) on ID — safe when that view is also one-row-per-patient (no duplication); use to combine additional admission-cohort attributes. | NOT safe to directly join to one-to-many tables/views such as examination_by_patient(SEL) or patient_admission_counts_by_sex(AGG) without re-aggregation, because those have multiple rows per patient and would multiply rows and duplicate the patient-level attributes from this view. Instead, aggregate the many-side first (for example: count or summarize examinations per ID) and then join the aggregated result back to this view on ID. | If you need metrics by Admission or Diagnosis (for example counts of patients per Admission), perform GROUP BY on Admission or Diagnosis after joining only to cardinality-safe sources (or after pre-aggregating many-side sources). That ensures measures derived from this view remain correct and are not inflated by join duplication.

views.description: Lists one row per patient with that patient's admission and primary diagnosis — useful for cohort selection and as a base for composing admission- or diagnosis-focused analyses.

views.name: patient_demographics_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Patient.ID AS ID,
  Patient.SEX AS SEX,
  Patient.Birthday AS Birthday,
  TRIM(NULLIF(Patient.Admission, '')) AS Admission,
  TRIM(NULLIF(Patient.Diagnosis, '')) AS Diagnosis,
  Patient."First Date" AS "First Date"
FROM Patient

params.description: Provides one-row-per-patient basic demographic and admission/diagnosis text fields (ID, sex, birthday, admission, diagnosis, first date).
params.when_to_use: Look up patient-level demographic attributes for a given patient ID or list of IDs. | Filter or join on patient-level attributes (SEX, Birthday, Admission, Diagnosis, First Date) as the driving patient grain in downstream queries. | Seed cohorts or build further patient-level aggregations (e.g., count of patients by sex or by admission/diagnosis) while preserving one-row-per-patient semantics.
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier; derives from Patient.ID | SEX: patient sex code/label; derives from Patient.SEX | Birthday: patient date of birth; derives from Patient.Birthday | Admission: trimmed Admission text (empty strings normalized to NULL); derives from Patient.Admission via TRIM(NULLIF(Patient.Admission, '')) | Diagnosis: trimmed Diagnosis text (empty strings normalized to NULL); derives from Patient.Diagnosis via TRIM(NULLIF(Patient.Diagnosis, '')) | First Date: first-date field for the patient; derives from Patient."First Date"
params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Patient.SEX | Patient.Birthday | Patient.Admission | Patient.Diagnosis | Patient."First Date"
params.metric: ID = Patient.ID | SEX = Patient.SEX | Birthday = Patient.Birthday | Admission = TRIM(NULLIF(Patient.Admission, '')) | Diagnosis = TRIM(NULLIF(Patient.Diagnosis, '')) | First Date = Patient."First Date"
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like one-row-per-patient views/tables on ID — for example, join to patient_basic_demographics (NORM) or sibling normalized patient views on patient ID — safe because patient_demographics_basic is one-row-per-patient, so joining on Patient.ID does not duplicate patient-level rows. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as examination_by_patient (SEL) or any raw events/encounters table that has multiple rows per patient without first aggregating those tables to one row per patient (e.g., counts, max/min dates) — direct join would multiply patient_demographics_basic rows and incorrectly inflate any patient-level measures. | When composing with patient_admission_counts_by_sex (AGG) or other aggregated-by-patient outputs, ensure the other side is aggregated to the same patient grain (one row per patient) or aggregated at a coarser grain (in which case join keys and semantics must be handled appropriately). | If you need patient-level metrics derived from many-to-one relationships (for example, latest exam date from examination_by_patient), pre-aggregate the many-side to patient ID (e.g., MAX(exam_date) GROUP BY patient_id) and then join to patient_demographics_basic on ID — this preserves cardinality and prevents duplication. | Safe join pattern example: FROM patient_demographics_basic p LEFT JOIN (SELECT patient_id, MAX(exam_date) AS last_exam FROM examination_by_patient GROUP BY patient_id) e ON p.ID = e.patient_id — safe because e is aggregated to one row per patient before joining. | Unsafe join pattern (avoid without aggregation): FROM patient_demographics_basic p JOIN examination_by_patient e ON p.ID = e.patient_id — unsafe because examination_by_patient is many-to-one and will duplicate p's row.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-patient basic demographic and admission/diagnosis text fields (ID, sex, birthday, admission, diagnosis, first date).

views.name: latest_examination_per_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT e.ID,
       e."Examination Date",
       e."aCL IgG",
       e."aCL IgM",
       e."ANA",
       e."ANA Pattern",
       e."aCL IgA",
       e."Diagnosis",
       e."Thrombosis"
FROM Examination e
JOIN (
  SELECT ID, MAX("Examination Date") AS max_date
  FROM Examination
  GROUP BY ID
) latest ON e.ID = latest.ID AND e."Examination Date" = latest.max_date

params.description: For each patient ID, returns the single most-recent Examination row (the latest examination date) and selected examination result fields.
params.when_to_use: Get the latest examination results per patient (e.g., most recent lab/serology values) for reporting or downstream joins. | Compose patient-level features that require only the most recent exam (e.g., latest ANA status, most recent aCL IgG) for modeling or cohort selection. | Join demographic or admission-level data to one row per patient without duplicating examination-derived measures.
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier — derived from Examination.ID (base column Examination.ID). | Examination Date: date/time of the examination — derived from Examination."Examination Date" (base column Examination."Examination Date"). | aCL IgG: aCL IgG test value recorded on that examination — derived from Examination."aCL IgG" (base column Examination."aCL IgG"). | aCL IgM: aCL IgM test value recorded on that examination — derived from Examination."aCL IgM" (base column Examination."aCL IgM"). | ANA: ANA test value recorded on that examination — derived from Examination."ANA" (base column Examination."ANA"). | ANA Pattern: ANA pattern recorded on that examination — derived from Examination."ANA Pattern" (base column Examination."ANA Pattern"). | aCL IgA: aCL IgA test value recorded on that examination — derived from Examination."aCL IgA" (base column Examination."aCL IgA"). | Diagnosis: diagnosis recorded on that examination — derived from Examination."Diagnosis" (base column Examination."Diagnosis"). | Thrombosis: thrombosis indicator recorded on that examination — derived from Examination."Thrombosis" (base column Examination."Thrombosis").
params.grounded_columns: Examination.ID | Examination."Examination Date" | Examination."aCL IgG" | Examination."aCL IgM" | Examination."ANA" | Examination."ANA Pattern" | Examination."aCL IgA" | Examination."Diagnosis" | Examination."Thrombosis"
params.metric: latest_examination_date = MAX(Examination."Examination Date") GROUP BY Examination.ID  -- used to pick the most recent row per ID | note: the view itself does not compute aggregates other than using the MAX in the internal subquery; all other output columns are passthroughs from the selected Examination row corresponding to that MAX.
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do not duplicate this view's measures): |  - Join to patient_basic_demographics (NORM) on ID = ID — safe because latest_examination_per_patient is one-row-per patient ID; joining to a one-row-per-ID demographics table will preserve one row per patient. |  - Join to patient_demographics_basic (NORM) on ID = ID — safe for the same reason as above. |  - Join to patient_admission_cohort (SEL) or female_patient_cohort (SEL) on ID = ID — safe if those cohort views are one-row-per patient ID; confirm those views' grain before joining. |  | Joins that can duplicate rows / require re-aggregation (unsafe to join directly if you want to preserve counts/measures): |  - Do NOT join directly to examination_by_patient (SEL) without aggregation, because examination_by_patient likely contains multiple examination rows per ID and will multiply rows/measures from this view. |  - Do NOT join directly to patient_admission_counts_by_sex (AGG) or any other view that is multi-row-per-ID (e.g., admissions where a patient can have multiple admissions) unless you aggregate the admission-side measures to one row per ID before joining. If you must join to a one-to-many view, either: |     * aggregate the many-side first to one row per ID (e.g., latest admission date, admission counts), or |     * join and then re-aggregate after the join, ensuring you use appropriate aggregation functions (e.g., MAX for dates, SUM for counts) so examination measures are not incorrectly multiplied. |  | Practical guidance for planners building on this view: |  - This view's grain is one row per Examination.ID (patient). It is safe to treat its columns as patient-level attributes. |  - If you need measures that combine latest examination values with admission-level measures that are multi-row per patient, compute the admission aggregation first (group by ID) and then join to latest_examination_per_patient on ID. |  - When composing additional derived metrics that count patients, count DISTINCT ID after joins to multi-row tables if you cannot control the other side's aggregation.

views.description: For each patient ID, returns the single most-recent Examination row (the latest examination date) and selected examination result fields.

views.name: patient_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Patient.ID AS "Patient.ID",
  Patient.SEX AS "Patient.SEX",
  Patient.Birthday AS "Patient.Birthday",
  Patient.Diagnosis AS "Patient.Diagnosis"
FROM Patient

params.description: Provides one-row-per-patient core demographic and diagnosis fields (ID, sex, birthday, diagnosis).
params.when_to_use: Look up basic patient attributes for a specific patient ID or small set of IDs | Join patient-level demographics to other patient-level or aggregated datasets | Seed cohorts or filters that require patient sex, birthdate, or diagnosis | Compose patient-level reports (e.g., compute age, stratify by sex, count patients by diagnosis) when counts/aggregates should be computed after joining or grouping
params.output_schema: Patient.ID: unique patient identifier — derived from Patient.ID (base table column) | Patient.SEX: patient sex/gender code — derived from Patient.SEX (base table column) | Patient.Birthday: patient date of birth — derived from Patient.Birthday (base table column) | Patient.Diagnosis: patient diagnosis code/label — derived from Patient.Diagnosis (base table column)
params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Patient.SEX | Patient.Birthday | Patient.Diagnosis
params.metric: No derived aggregate metrics in this view; all outputs are direct base columns (identity projections). If you need metrics, compute them on top of this view, e.g., patient_age = DATE_PART('year', CURRENT_DATE) - DATE_PART('year', Patient.Birthday) computed by the consumer.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_demographics_basic (NORM) on Patient.ID — safe because both views are normalized per patient (one-row-per-ID), so joining preserves one row per patient and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_basic_demographics (NORM) on Patient.ID — safe for the same reason: both are one-row-per-patient normalized views. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_examination_per_patient (RANK) on Patient.ID — safe because latest_examination_per_patient is one-row-per-patient (ranked to latest), so it will not multiply rows when joined 1:1 by Patient.ID. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many views/tables such as examination_by_patient (SEL), patient_admission_cohort (SEL), patient_admission_counts_by_sex (AGG), patient_cohort_by_admission_and_diagnosis (SEL), female_patient_cohort (SEL) without first aggregating those views to patient-level — joining to these one-to-many sources will multiply patient_core rows and thus duplicate any patient-level measures. Instead, aggregate the child side to one row per Patient.ID (e.g., COUNT(*) AS exam_count GROUP BY Patient.ID) and then join on Patient.ID. | When composing metrics that count patients (e.g., number of patients by diagnosis or sex), perform aggregation after any joins that could introduce multiplicity, or use DISTINCT Patient.ID in the aggregation to avoid double-counting if joins to many-side tables are unavoidable. | If you need to join on other keys, ensure the other view/table is also one-row-per-Patient.ID (or pre-aggregated to that grain). Any join to a table with >1 row per Patient.ID will require re-aggregation on Patient.ID to preserve correct patient-level measures.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-patient core demographic and diagnosis fields (ID, sex, birthday, diagnosis).

views.name: laboratory_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "Laboratory"."ID" AS "Laboratory.ID",
  "Laboratory"."Date" AS "Laboratory.Date"
FROM "Laboratory"

params.description: Provides the canonical set of laboratory event rows at the grain of Laboratory.ID and Laboratory.Date (one row per laboratory event).
params.when_to_use: List or filter laboratory events (by ID, date, or predicates on those columns). | Join laboratory events to patient- or admission-level dimensions when you need event-level detail without aggregated measures. | Use as the base when composing aggregations (counts, distinct counts, min/max dates) over laboratory events.

params.grounded_columns: Laboratory.ID | Laboratory.Date
params.metric: count_events = COUNT(Laboratory.ID)  -- a valid aggregation when this view is grouped; Laboratory.ID is the event identifier used for counts | distinct_events = COUNT(DISTINCT Laboratory.ID)  -- distinct count of event identifiers | min_event_date = MIN(Laboratory.Date)  -- earliest event date in a group | max_event_date = MAX(Laboratory.Date)  -- latest event date in a group
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_demographics_basic (or patient_core or patient_basic_demographics) on the patient identifier column only if there is a one-to-one relationship between Laboratory.ID and that patient key in the schema (this view itself does not expose a patient key; include the patient key in an extended projection before joining). Safe when joining on a one-row-per-patient key because laboratory event rows will align to a single patient row without duplicating patient-level measures. | do NOT join this view directly to any table/view that is one-to-many relative to Laboratory.ID (for example, if there is a separate measurements table that contains multiple measurement-values per Laboratory.ID) without re-aggregating the measurements first. Joining a one-to-many child will multiply the number of rows per Laboratory.ID and thus inflate raw counts derived from this view. | when composing aggregations across relationships: if you need patient-level aggregates (e.g., number of lab events per patient), GROUP BY the patient key after joining Laboratory (or better: first join to a mapping that maps Laboratory.ID→patient_id as a one-to-one relation), then aggregate. Avoid relying on this view to implicitly preserve uniqueness across joins; explicitly aggregate (COUNT(DISTINCT Laboratory.ID)) when joining to many-sided tables. | joining to sibling SELECT-level views (e.g., examination_by_patient, latest_examination_per_patient) is safe only if those sibling views are at a compatible grain and the join keys represent one-to-one correspondence. If sibling view grain is coarser (per patient or per admission), either aggregate laboratory_events to that grain first or use DISTINCT/COUNT(DISTINCT Laboratory.ID) to prevent duplication. | example safe composition: to get daily lab-event counts, SELECT Laboratory.Date, COUNT(Laboratory.ID) FROM laboratory_events GROUP BY Laboratory.Date — safe because aggregation is performed at this view's native grain. | example unsafe composition: SELECT p.*, COUNT(Laboratory.ID) FROM laboratory_events JOIN measurements m ON m.Laboratory_ID = Laboratory.ID JOIN patients p ON p.ID = m.Patient_ID GROUP BY p.ID — unsafe unless you aggregate measurements per Laboratory.ID first, because the join to measurements may produce multiple rows per Laboratory.ID and inflate counts.

params.description: Provides one row per patient lab event (patient ID + laboratory date) with the patient's diagnosis — useful for analyses that need patient-level lab event records combined with diagnosis.
params.when_to_use: Count or list laboratory events per patient or per date where you also need the patient's diagnosis. | Filter laboratory events by patient diagnosis and then aggregate (e.g., number of lab events by diagnosis or by date). | Compose into cohorts that require the lab event date and patient diagnosis (for cohort selection or downstream joins that will not multiply rows).
params.output_schema: Patient.ID: patient identifier — derived from Patient.ID in the base Patient table (aliased as Patient.ID in the view). | Patient.Diagnosis: patient diagnosis/category — derived from Patient.Diagnosis in the base Patient table (aliased as Patient.Diagnosis in the view). | Laboratory.Date: date of the laboratory event — derived from Laboratory.Date in the base Laboratory table (aliased as Laboratory.Date in the view).
params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Patient.Diagnosis | Laboratory.Date | Laboratory.ID
params.metric: No native aggregated metrics are defined in this view. The view exposes the raw columns: Patient.ID, Patient.Diagnosis, Laboratory.Date. Any metrics (counts, distinct counts, rates) must be defined by aggregating these columns in a consuming query or view. Examples of common derived metrics consumers will build on this view: | lab_event_count = COUNT(*)  -- counts rows (one row per joined Patient-Laboratory event) | distinct_patient_count = COUNT(DISTINCT Patient.ID)  -- counts unique patients in the result set | lab_events_by_date = COUNT(*) GROUP BY Laboratory.Date
params.composition: Safe joins (do not duplicate this view's measures): join to patient-level 1:1 or many-to-1 views/tables keyed by Patient.ID, because patient_lab_join is at the grain of (Patient.ID, Laboratory.Date) and the patient-level view/table will collapse to one row per Patient.ID. Examples: |   - Join to patient_basic_demographics on Patient.ID — safe because that view is patient-level (NORM), one row per patient, so each (Patient.ID, Laboratory.Date) row matches at most one demographic row and measures (e.g., COUNT(*)) remain correct. |   - Join to patient_demographics_basic or patient_core on Patient.ID — safe for the same reason (these are normalized patient-level sources). | Unsafe joins (would multiply rows / require re-aggregation): do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many detail tables or views keyed at the event-level or admission-level without re-aggregation, because those joins can duplicate lab-event rows and inflate counts. Examples: |   - Do NOT directly join to examination_by_patient (SEL) if it contains multiple examination rows per patient, unless you aggregate examination_by_patient to one row per Patient.ID first (e.g., latest_examination_per_patient or an aggregation). |   - Do NOT directly join to laboratory_events (SEL) if it contains multiple laboratory event rows per patient/date that are distinct from the rows already represented here — joining may duplicate rows unless you join on the exact same event key and it is guaranteed 1:1. |   - Do NOT directly join to patient_admission_counts_by_sex (AGG) only if that AGG is at a different grain (such as counts per patient aggregated by sex) without ensuring the join key is compatible; if the aggregate is at patient-level (one row per patient) it is safe, but if at sex-level (one row per sex) joining would broadcast counts incorrectly. | Guidance for safe composition and preserving measure correctness: |   - When joining to a dimension/view that is one-row-per-Patient.ID (patient-level), join ON Patient.ID — safe because patient_lab_join is at a finer grain (patient+date) and the patient dimension is many-to-one into this view. |   - When joining to another event-level view, ensure you join on the full event key (if present) that yields a 1:1 match, or first aggregate the other view to the (Patient.ID, Laboratory.Date) grain (or to Patient.ID if that is the intended grain) before joining. |   - If you need to combine this view with an admission-level or exam-level table that is many-to-many with lab events, first aggregate the admission/exam table to Patient.ID (or to Patient.ID + Date if that is the intended combined grain), then join. Alternatively, perform analytic/partitioned joins that deduplicate before aggregating. | Examples of safe compositions: |   - Counting lab events by diagnosis: SELECT Patient.Diagnosis, COUNT(*) FROM patient_lab_join GROUP BY Patient.Diagnosis |   - Enrich lab events with patient demographics: SELECT l.*, d.age FROM patient_lab_join l JOIN patient_basic_demographics d ON l.Patient.ID = d.ID | Examples of unsafe composition without re-aggregation: |   - SELECT l.Patient.ID, COUNT(*) FROM patient_lab_join l JOIN examination_by_patient e ON l.Patient.ID = e.ID GROUP BY l.Patient.ID  -- unsafe if examination_by_patient has multiple rows per patient; counts will be multiplied unless e is pre-aggregated.

If the other view is not guaranteed one-row-per-(ID, Date), either aggregate it to that grain or join on ID only and then re-aggregate as needed. | Avoid joining laboratory_records to patient_admission_counts_by_sex(AGG) or other aggregated-by-ID summary tables and then treating rows as distinct lab events without re-aggregation, because aggregated tables may represent counts or summaries and could cause semantic errors if combined improperly — instead, join for dimension attributes or compute metrics separately and combine in a controlled aggregation step.

Because this view exposes only examination-level rows, joining directly to a one-row-per-patient table is safe only if you first aggregate examinations to one row per patient (e.g., latest_examination_per_patient) or have a patient key in both sides. |  - Join to latest_examination_per_patient (RANK) on ID = ID — safe because latest_examination_per_patient is one-row-per-patient and if you join this view to it by examination ID, the latest_examination_per_patient will match at most one row (the latest exam) so measures are not duplicated. | Do NOT join without care to one-to-many tables/views that relate multiple rows per examination (these would duplicate examination-level rows/measures): |  - Do NOT join directly to laboratory_events (SEL) or laboratory_records (SEL) on Examination.ID (or on an examination->lab foreign key) unless you intend to expand examination rows by lab events. views.name: patient_demographics_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  P.ID AS ID,
  P.SEX AS SEX,
  -- ISO format dates: assume stored as DATE; use SQLite's date() to canonicalize
  CASE
    WHEN length(Description) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE date(Description)
  END AS Description_iso,
  CASE
    WHEN length(Birthday) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE date(Birthday)
  END AS Birthday_iso,
  -- canonicalize Admission codes: map common variants to canonical set {ADMIT, DISCH, UNKNOWN}
  CASE
    WHEN Admission IN ('+', 'ADMIT', 'Admit', 'admit', 'A') THEN 'ADMITTED'
    WHEN Admission IN ('-', 'DISCH', 'Disch', 'disch', 'D') THEN 'DISCHARGED'
    WHEN Admission IS NULL OR trim(Admission) = '' THEN 'UNKNOWN'
    ELSE upper(Admission)
  END AS Admission_canonical,
  CASE
    WHEN length("First Date") = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE date("First Date")
  END AS First_Date_iso,
  -- keep Diagnosis verbatim from Patient table for canonical demographics
  P.Diagnosis AS Diagnosis
FROM Patient P

params.when_to_use: Lookup a patient's normalized demographics (sex, birthday, description date) by patient ID. | Filter or cohort patients by canonical admission status (ADMITTED / DISCHARGED / UNKNOWN) or by Diagnosis. | Base dataset for joining patient-level attributes into analyses that compute aggregates per patient (e.g., counts of patients, patient-level cohorts). | Compose higher-level SQL that needs ISO-normalized dates (Description_iso, Birthday_iso, First_Date_iso) for date arithmetic or comparisons.
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier, derived from Patient.ID | SEX: patient sex as stored, derived from Patient.SEX | Description_iso: Description converted to ISO DATE (YYYY-MM-DD) or NULL when empty, derived from Patient.Description via date(Description) with empty-string->NULL rule | Birthday_iso: Birthday converted to ISO DATE or NULL when empty, derived from Patient.Birthday via date(Birthday) with empty-string->NULL rule | Admission_canonical: canonical admission status mapped to one of {ADMITTED, DISCHARGED, UNKNOWN} or uppercased Admission otherwise; derived from Patient.Admission with mappings for common variants | First_Date_iso: "First Date" field converted to ISO DATE or NULL when empty, derived from Patient."First Date" via date("First Date") with empty-string->NULL rule | Diagnosis: diagnosis verbatim, derived from Patient.Diagnosis
params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Patient.SEX | Patient.Description | Patient.Birthday | Patient.Admission | Patient.First Date | Patient.Diagnosis
params.metric: Description_iso = CASE WHEN length(Description) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE date(Description) END | Birthday_iso = CASE WHEN length(Birthday) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE date(Birthday) END | Admission_canonical = CASE WHEN Admission IN ('+', 'ADMIT', 'Admit', 'admit', 'A') THEN 'ADMITTED' WHEN Admission IN ('-', 'DISCH', 'Disch', 'disch', 'D') THEN 'DISCHARGED' WHEN Admission IS NULL OR trim(Admission) = '' THEN 'UNKNOWN' ELSE upper(Admission) END | First_Date_iso = CASE WHEN length("First Date") = 0 THEN NULL ELSE date("First Date") END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like patient-level views/tables on ID — safe because patient_demographics_normalized is one-row-per-ID (grain = [ID]) so its columns are not duplicated. Example: JOIN patient_demographics_normalized N ON N.ID = patient_core.ID | do NOT directly join to one-to-many event tables/views (e.g., laboratory_events, examination_by_patient, laboratory_records, patient_admission_counts_by_sex) without aggregation or selecting a single row per patient first, because those joins will multiply patient_demographics_normalized rows and thus duplicate patient-level measures unless you aggregate the many-side first. Instead: aggregate events to patient-level (e.g., MAX(date), COUNT(*)) or use latest_examination_per_patient (which is rank-reduced to one row per patient) before joining. | When composing aggregates: if you need patient counts or patient-level metrics, aggregate after joining (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT N.ID) for unique patients) or aggregate event tables to patient granularity and then join to this view to preserve correct measures. | Safe joins examples: JOIN patient_core ON ID, JOIN patient_demographics_basic ON ID, JOIN patient_basic_demographics ON ID — these are patient-level (NORM) views and will not multiply rows. | Unsafe joins without re-aggregation: JOIN laboratory_events LE ON N.ID = LE.ID (unsafe) — this will produce one output row per lab event per patient and duplicate patient-level attributes; instead use a subquery that aggregates laboratory_events by ID first (e.g., SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS lab_count FROM laboratory_events GROUP BY ID) and then join.

views.body_sql:
SELECT
  P.ID AS ID,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(E."Examination Date" ) FILTER (WHERE E."Symptoms" IS NOT NULL) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_symptom_examination,
  COALESCE(COUNT(E."Examination Date") FILTER (WHERE E."Symptoms" IS NOT NULL), 0) AS symptom_exam_count,
  MIN(E."Examination Date") FILTER (WHERE E."Symptoms" IS NOT NULL) AS first_symptom_exam_date,

GROUP BY P.ID

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient-level normalized views/tables (one-row-per-patient) on ID — e.g., join to patient_core (NORM) or patient_demographics_basic (NORM) ON ID — safe because latest_laboratory_date_per_patient has exactly one row per Patient.ID (the view groups by Patient.ID), so measures (latest_lab_date) will not be duplicated. | Do NOT join this AGG view directly to tables or views that are one-to-many with respect to Patient.ID (for example: laboratory_events (SEL), laboratory_records (SEL), patient_admission_cohort (if it is one-to-many per patient), examination_by_patient (SEL) if it yields multiple rows per patient, or patient_lab_join (JOIN) that produces multiple lab rows) without re-aggregation or first reducing those children to one-row-per-patient. Joining to a one-to-many child will multiply rows and will not preserve the single aggregated value semantics. | If you need to combine latest_lab_date with another one-to-many measure (for example, count of admissions per patient), either: (a) aggregate the one-to-many side to patient-level before joining (e.g., admissions_per_patient = COUNT(*) GROUP BY ID), then join patient-level aggregates to this view on ID; or (b) join and then re-aggregate at the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY Patient.ID and recompute necessary aggregates). | When computing derived time metrics (e.g., days between latest_lab_date and admission_date), ensure joins are at patient-level or that you compute the time difference after reducing other tables to patient-level, so the date value is not duplicated and the arithmetic remains correct. | Because the view uses LEFT JOIN Laboratory ON Laboratory.ID = Patient.ID and groups by Patient.ID, patients without any Laboratory rows will appear with latest_lab_date = NULL. Be explicit about NULL handling when composing (e.g., treat NULL as 'no labs' or impute a default if needed).

views.name: patient_has_abnormal_ua
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID AS ID,
  p.SEX AS sex,
  q.abnormal_threshold AS abnormal_threshold,
  CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN l.UA > q.abnormal_threshold THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_abnormal_ua
FROM
  patient_basic_demographics p
LEFT JOIN
  laboratory_ua_records l
  ON p.ID = l.ID
-- question_ops parameter table alias q provides the threshold value; this view expects q.abnormal_threshold to be supplied when used
CROSS JOIN
  (SELECT CAST(NULL AS REAL) AS abnormal_threshold) q
GROUP BY
  p.ID, p.SEX, q.abnormal_threshold

params.description: For each patient and sex, indicates whether that patient has at least one urine analyte (UA) measurement strictly greater than a provided abnormal_threshold.
params.when_to_use: Determine whether individual patients had any UA measurement above a configurable threshold. | Filter or cohort patients by presence/absence of abnormal UA (binary flag) using a supplied abnormal_threshold parameter. | Compose patient-level binary abnormal-UA indicators into higher-level aggregates (counts, rates) by grouping after joining safely. | Build downstream SQL that needs a patient-level boolean flag of abnormal UA relative to a dynamic threshold (passed in as question_ops/parameter).
params.output_schema: ID: patient identifier; derived from patient_basic_demographics.ID | sex: patient sex/gender field; derived from patient_basic_demographics.SEX | abnormal_threshold: the numeric threshold value against which UA is compared; supplied by caller via q.abnormal_threshold (question_ops parameter); represented in the view as CAST(NULL AS REAL) placeholder but expected to be provided at runtime | has_abnormal_ua: binary indicator (1/0) equal to 1 if the patient has at least one laboratory_ua_records.UA > abnormal_threshold, else 0; computed via an aggregate over laboratory_ua_records.UA
params.grounded_columns: patient_basic_demographics.ID | patient_basic_demographics.SEX | laboratory_ua_records.ID | laboratory_ua_records.UA
params.metric: has_abnormal_ua = CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN laboratory_ua_records.UA > abnormal_threshold THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | Note: the inner CASE produces 1 for each UA row exceeding the provided abnormal_threshold; MAX(...) over the patient's UA rows yields 1 if any row exceeds the threshold, otherwise 0.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient-level dimension or normalized patient views (one-row-per-patient) such as patient_basic_demographics, patient_demographics_basic, patient_core on ID — safe because patient_has_abnormal_ua is one row per patient (grain: ID, sex, abnormal_threshold) so joining on ID will not duplicate measures. | You may join to aggregated patient-level cohorts or selection views (e.g., patient_admission_cohort, female_patient_cohort) on ID or ID+SEX provided those are one-row-per-patient; confirm those siblings are one-row-per-patient before joining without re-aggregation. | Do NOT directly join patient_has_abnormal_ua to tables or views that are one-to-many per patient (e.g., laboratory_events, laboratory_records, examination_by_patient, latest_examination_per_patient if multiple rows per patient are present) without first aggregating those tables to patient-level. Such joins would multiply rows and duplicate the binary measure, invalidating counts and sums unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If composing higher-level metrics (counts, rates) from has_abnormal_ua, aggregate after joining: e.g., SELECT sex, abnormal_threshold, SUM(has_abnormal_ua) AS patients_with_abnormal_ua, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patient_has_abnormal_ua GROUP BY sex, abnormal_threshold. | When supplying abnormal_threshold parameter: ensure the planner supplies a single scalar abnormal_threshold value (via question_ops parameter binding) or a table that preserves the one-row-per-patient grain (the view currently CROSS JOINs a q subquery placeholder). If multiple thresholds are supplied (multiple rows in q), the view will produce one row per patient per threshold — this is intentional when evaluating multiple thresholds but be aware this increases cardinality accordingly. | If you need patient-admission-level or event-level joins, first expand/aggregate patient_has_abnormal_ua to the appropriate grain or re-compute the abnormal-UA logic at that grain to avoid double counting.

params.description: Provides one row per examination with patient demographic fields (birthday, sex) and examination attributes (diagnosis, thrombosis) — answers questions about examinations enriched with basic patient demographics.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve examination-level details along with the patient's birthday and sex for reporting or filtering. | Filter or cohort examinations by patient demographics (e.g., sex or age at examination) while preserving the examination granularity. | Build downstream aggregates per examination (e.g., count of examinations by diagnosis or thrombosis status) where each examination must be counted once. | Join examination-level analyses to other one-row-per-patient or one-row-per-examination dimensions safely (see composition guidance).
params.output_schema: Examination.ID: unique identifier of the examination — sourced from Examination.ID | Examination.Examination Date: date/time of the examination — sourced from Examination."Examination Date" | Patient.Birthday: patient's date of birth — sourced from Patient.Birthday | Patient.SEX: patient's sex/gender code/value — sourced from Patient.SEX | Examination.Diagnosis: diagnosis associated with the examination — sourced from Examination.Diagnosis | Examination.Thrombosis: thrombosis flag/indicator for the examination — sourced from Examination.Thrombosis
params.grounded_columns: Examination.ID | Examination.Examination Date | Examination.Diagnosis | Examination.Thrombosis | Patient.ID | Patient.Birthday | Patient.SEX
params.metric: There are no aggregated metrics in this view; all outputs are direct column projections at the examination grain. | If you need derived metrics, compute them on top of this view. Example safe derived metrics (computed per-examination): | age_at_examination = DATE_PART('year', Examination.Examination Date) - DATE_PART('year', Patient.Birthday)  -- example expression to compute age (SQL dialect may vary) | is_thrombosis = Examination.Thrombosis  -- treat as a boolean or categorical flag depending on source type
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-patient dimensions/views on Patient.ID (or Examination.ID when joining to examination-keyed views) — safe because this view is one-row-per-examination and the join preserves that granularity. | Examples of SAFE joins: | Join to patient_core or patient_demographics_basic on Patient.ID — safe because those views are normalized patient-level (one row per Patient.ID), so each examination row remains one row and measures are not duplicated. | Join to latest_examination_per_patient on Examination.ID or Patient.ID depending on that view's key only when semantics align (ensure the target view is one-row-per-examination or one-row-per-patient as required). | UNSAFE joins (will duplicate this view's rows/measures unless you re-aggregate): | Do NOT directly join this view to any one-to-many tables/views such as laboratory_events, laboratory_records, patient_admission_counts_by_sex (aggregated counts by patient dimension may be safe only if pre-aggregated to one row per patient), patient_lab_join, or other event-level tables without re-aggregation because those joins will multiply examination rows when multiple matching rows exist per Patient.ID or Examination.ID. | If you must combine with one-to-many data, either: | - aggregate the many-side beforehand to one row per Examination.ID or Patient.ID (e.g., lab counts per examination or per patient), then join; or | - join and then re-aggregate at the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY Examination.ID) to avoid inflated counts/measures. | When composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., count of examinations with thrombosis by sex), aggregate over Examination.ID from this view — that preserves correct counts because the view's grain is Examination.ID + Examination.Examination Date.

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_demographics_basic (or any one-row-per-ID dimension) on ID — safe because patient_demographics_basic is one row per ID, so joining will not duplicate laboratory_row_level rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_core (or other patient-level normalized views) on ID — safe because those views are one-row-per-ID; laboratory_row_level remains the detailed, one-row-per-(ID,Date) fact. | do NOT join directly to laboratory_events or laboratory_records (one-to-many to this view) without re-aggregating first — those sibling views may represent multiple event/detail rows per (ID, Date) and would multiply HGB rows/measure semantics if joined directly. | do NOT join directly to examination_by_patient or latest_examination_per_patient expecting preservation of one-row-per-(ID,Date) unless you verify their grain and that they are one-row-per-ID-or-date; joining on ID only may duplicate HGB if the other view has multiple rows per ID. | When composing aggregations (e.g., average HGB per patient or per date), aggregate HGB in queries built on this view (e.g., GROUP BY ID to get per-patient mean(HGB)) rather than joining to a table with multiple rows per (ID,Date) which would require de-duplication or pre-aggregation. | If you need patient-admission-level context (patient_admission_cohort), join on ID and an admission date range condition that maps Laboratory.Date into the admission interval; ensure admission cohort is one-row-per-admission and that the join condition is a one-to-many relationship from admissions to lab rows (admission will be duplicated across labs) — this is acceptable only if you intend to count/aggregate lab rows per admission. | To preserve correct measures when combining with one-to-many siblings, either: (a) aggregate laboratory_row_level first to the desired grain (e.g., per ID or per ID+admission) and then join, or (b) join and then apply GROUP BY with appropriate aggregation functions on HGB to remove duplication.

params.description: Provides one row per patient examination date, listing the patient ID, the examination date, and the recorded diagnosis for that examination.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve examinations at the per-patient-per-date grain (e.g., list all diagnoses by patient and exam date). | Compose queries that need a stable per-examination row to join to other patient-level or event-level data without duplicating examination rows. | Filter, aggregate, or pivot diagnoses by examination date (for example: count examinations per diagnosis per date). | Serve as the detailed input when building summaries of examinations (must re-aggregate after joining to many-side tables).

params.grounded_columns: Examination.ID | Examination."Examination Date" | Examination."Diagnosis"
params.metric: ID = identity(Examination.ID) | Examination Date = identity(Examination."Examination Date") | Diagnosis = identity(Examination."Diagnosis")
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient-level (one-row-per-patient) views on ID — e.g., join to patient_core(ID) or patient_demographics_basic(ID) — safe because those are one-row-per-patient so they will not multiply examination rows (each examination remains one row). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_examination_per_patient on (ID, "Examination Date") only if latest_examination_per_patient is one-row-per-(ID,Examination Date); verify its grain first. If it is one-row-per-patient, do NOT join directly because that would collapse multiple examination rows per patient. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many event or measurement tables (e.g., laboratory_events, laboratory_records, patient_lab_join) without re-aggregation on the many-side first, because those tables have multiple rows per examination or per patient and would duplicate examination rows and any counts/measures derived from this view. Instead, aggregate the many-side to the examination grain (ID + Examination Date) or patient grain, then join. | When joining to sibling selection or cohort views (e.g., patient_admission_cohort, female_patient_cohort, patient_cohort_by_admission_and_diagnosis), ensure you understand their grain: if they are one-row-per-patient, joining on ID is safe; if they are one-row-per-admission, avoid joining directly on ID+Examination Date unless you first align grains (e.g., map examinations to admissions). | If you need to compute aggregates over examinations after joining further details, perform the aggregation after the join and GROUP BY the examination grain (ID, Examination Date) or a coarser grain as appropriate — do not assume measures remain unique after joining many-side tables. | Summary: safe to join on ID to patient-level (1:1) dims; avoid direct joins to laboratory_events, laboratory_records, or other event-level (1:N) tables without pre-aggregation to the examination (ID, Examination Date) or patient (ID) grain to prevent measure duplication.

params.description: Provides a denormalized patient-level + examination-level join that lists each examination row with patient identifying and diagnosis information (one row per patient examination).

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to Patient (or patient-level normalized views such as patient_basic_demographics, patient_demographics_basic, patient_core) on ID — safe because Patient (and those normalized patient-level views) are one-row-per-patient and this view is one-row-per-examination (a many-to-one join from this view to patient-level dims will not duplicate examination rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_examination_per_patient on (ID, Examination Date) or on ID with appropriate filtering — safe only if the target view provides at most one row per (ID, Examination Date) or one row per ID respectively. When joining to latest_examination_per_patient on ID (one-row-per-patient), be aware you may filter this view's examination rows down to the latest exam if you inner join; it will not multiplicatively duplicate measures. | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables/views that contain multiple rows per examination (for example: laboratory_events or laboratory_records when they have multiple lab events per Examination row) without first aggregating the many-side to the examination grain. Joining directly to a many-to-many or one-to-many child (laboratory_events) will multiply examination rows and thereby duplicate counts/metrics derived from this view. | do NOT join to patient_admission_counts_by_sex or other aggregated views that are at a different grain unless you understand their aggregation keys. If joining to an aggregated view, either join on exactly-matching grain keys (so no duplication) or re-aggregate after the join to preserve correct measures. | When composing further aggregations on top of this view (e.g., COUNT(examinations) by Patient.Diagnosis or by Examination Date), treat this view as the base at the examination grain: aggregate using GROUP BY over ID and/or Examination Date as required. If you need patient-level aggregates (one row per patient), first aggregate this view to one row per patient (for example, using MAX/COUNT/last exam logic) before joining to other patient-level dimensions to avoid double-counting. | If joining to other JOIN views (e.g., patient_lab_join), ensure the other view's grain is compatible: it must be either one-row-per-examination or pre-aggregated to the examination grain to be safe without further aggregation.

views.name: laboratory_row
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Laboratory.ID AS ID,
  Laboratory.Date AS Date,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(Laboratory.GPT)='' OR Laboratory.GPT IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(Laboratory.GPT AS REAL)
  END AS GPT,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(Laboratory.ALB)='' OR Laboratory.ALB IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(Laboratory.ALB AS REAL)
  END AS ALB,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(Laboratory.GOT)='' OR Laboratory.GOT IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(Laboratory.GOT AS REAL)
  END AS GOT,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(Laboratory.LDH)='' OR Laboratory.LDH IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(Laboratory.LDH AS REAL)
  END AS LDH,
  -- CRP is stored as TEXT in schema; normalize common numeric-looking values to REAL, keep NULL otherwise
  CASE
    WHEN Laboratory.CRP IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN trim(Laboratory.CRP)='' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- try to cast numeric textual CRP to real; SQLite returns 0 for non-numeric cast via plus operator, so use +0.0 only when text looks like number via LIKE
      CASE
        WHEN Laboratory.CRP GLOB '[0-9]*' OR Laboratory.CRP GLOB '[0-9]*.[0-9]*' OR Laboratory.CRP GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN CAST(Laboratory.CRP AS REAL)
        ELSE NULL
      END
  END AS CRP
FROM Laboratory

params.description: Provides one laboratory row per Laboratory.ID and Date with normalized numeric lab values (GPT, ALB, GOT, LDH, CRP).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve normalized numeric laboratory test values for a specific laboratory record (by ID and Date). | Compose time-series or per-record analyses where each row should represent a single Laboratory.ID x Date measurement. | Join laboratory measurements to patient or admission-level entities when you need one row per lab record and want numeric casts/NULLs for non-numeric or empty values. | Use as a base to aggregate lab metrics (e.g., mean GPT per patient, min/max CRP by admission) after grouping — do not assume aggregates are already computed here.
params.output_schema: ID: unique identifier of the laboratory record, from Laboratory.ID | Date: date/time of the laboratory record, from Laboratory.Date | GPT: alanine aminotransferase value (normalized to REAL). Derived from Laboratory.GPT with empty-string and NULL mapped to NULL; otherwise CAST(Laboratory.GPT AS REAL). | ALB: albumin value (normalized to REAL). Derived from Laboratory.ALB with empty-string and NULL mapped to NULL; otherwise CAST(Laboratory.ALB AS REAL). | GOT: aspartate aminotransferase value (normalized to REAL). Derived from Laboratory.GOT with empty-string and NULL mapped to NULL; otherwise CAST(Laboratory.GOT AS REAL). | LDH: lactate dehydrogenase value (normalized to REAL). Derived from Laboratory.LDH with empty-string and NULL mapped to NULL; otherwise CAST(Laboratory.LDH AS REAL). | CRP: C-reactive protein normalized to REAL when textual contents look numeric; Laboratory.CRP NULL or empty-string become NULL; non-numeric text becomes NULL. Numeric detection uses GLOB patterns and then CAST(Laboratory.CRP AS REAL).
params.grounded_columns: Laboratory.ID | Laboratory.Date | Laboratory.GPT | Laboratory.ALB | Laboratory.GOT | Laboratory.LDH | Laboratory.CRP
params.metric: GPT = CASE WHEN trim(Laboratory.GPT)='' OR Laboratory.GPT IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(Laboratory.GPT AS REAL) END | ALB = CASE WHEN trim(Laboratory.ALB)='' OR Laboratory.ALB IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(Laboratory.ALB AS REAL) END | GOT = CASE WHEN trim(Laboratory.GOT)='' OR Laboratory.GOT IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(Laboratory.GOT AS REAL) END | LDH = CASE WHEN trim(Laboratory.LDH)='' OR Laboratory.LDH IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(Laboratory.LDH AS REAL) END | CRP = CASE WHEN Laboratory.CRP IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN trim(Laboratory.CRP)='' THEN NULL ELSE CASE WHEN Laboratory.CRP GLOB '[0-9]*' OR Laboratory.CRP GLOB '[0-9]*.[0-9]*' OR Laboratory.CRP GLOB '*[0-9]*' THEN CAST(Laboratory.CRP AS REAL) ELSE NULL END END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to patient_core (or any patient-level NORM view keyed 1:1 to the Laboratory's patient identifier) on the laboratory->patient key (NOT present in this view's outputs; use Laboratory.ID mapping via patient_lab_join or laboratory_events if you need patient keys) only if that target is one-row-per-patient and you join on the patient key — safe because laboratory_row is one row per laboratory ID x Date and joining to a single row per patient will not duplicate these lab rows' measures. | Do NOT directly join laboratory_row to one-to-many tables/views such as examination_by_patient, laboratory_records, laboratory_events, patient_admission_counts_by_sex, or any other view that can contain multiple rows per the same Laboratory.ID (or per the same patient and date) without first aggregating or deduplicating those many-side rows. Such joins would multiply laboratory_row rows/measures and lead to incorrect totals or averages. | If you need to combine with a one-to-many relation (for example, multiple examinations or multiple admissions per lab record), first aggregate the many-side to one row per Laboratory.ID (or per patient+Date) using an appropriate aggregate (e.g., MAX, MIN, COUNT, AVG) and then join on (Laboratory.ID) or (patient key + Date) to preserve cardinality. | When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., average GPT per patient), perform GROUP BY on the appropriate patient identifier after joining laboratory_row to a patient-level key or by using patient_lab_join (which maps lab rows to patients) and then aggregating; do not sum or average across joins that may have duplicated lab rows. | This view is normalized to the grain [ID, Date]. Any join must respect that grain: joining to another dataset at the same grain (Laboratory.ID, Date) is safe; joining to datasets at a broader grain (patient or admission) is safe only if the broader-side is 1:1 for the matching key, otherwise aggregate the broader-side first to avoid duplication.

views.name: patient_examination_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID AS ID,
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = p.ID AND e.Thrombosis IS NOT NULL AND e.Thrombosis != 0
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_thrombosis_values,
  (
    SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT TRIM(e."ANA Pattern")) FROM Examination e
    WHERE e.ID = p.ID AND e."ANA Pattern" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(e."ANA Pattern") <> ''
  ) AS distinct_ana_patterns,
  (
    SELECT MAX(e."aCL IgM") FROM Examination e
    WHERE e.ID = p.ID AND e."aCL IgM" IS NOT NULL
  ) AS max_aCL_IgM,
  (
    SELECT MIN(e."aCL IgM") FROM Examination e
    WHERE e.ID = p.ID AND e."aCL IgM" IS NOT NULL
  ) AS min_aCL_IgM,
  (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination e
    WHERE e.ID = p.ID
  ) AS count_exams
FROM Patient p

params.grounded_columns: Patient.ID | Examination.ID | Examination.Thrombosis | Examination."ANA Pattern" | Examination."aCL IgM"
params.metric: has_thrombosis_values = CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = Patient.ID AND e.Thrombosis IS NOT NULL AND e.Thrombosis != 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | distinct_ana_patterns = (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT TRIM(e."ANA Pattern")) FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = Patient.ID AND e."ANA Pattern" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(e."ANA Pattern") <> '') | max_aCL_IgM = (SELECT MAX(e."aCL IgM") FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = Patient.ID AND e."aCL IgM" IS NOT NULL) | min_aCL_IgM = (SELECT MIN(e."aCL IgM") FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = Patient.ID AND e."aCL IgM" IS NOT NULL) | count_exams = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = Patient.ID)
